name: Disclosure
summary: A disclosure is a button that shows and hides the region right after it. Use it to keep detail out of the way until someone asks for it. The state belongs to the button as `aria-expanded`, and the panel has to leave the accessibility tree when it closes, not only the screen.
demoNote: Example 5's panel says it is closed and still holds a link in the tab order. Everything under Common mistakes is live.

contract.useWhen: A button that shows and hides the region right after it.
keyboard: native: moves to the trigger, then into the panel when it is open
native: toggles. It is a <button>, so there is no key handler to write
nothing, deliberately. A disclosure does not trap focus, so Esc stays with whatever surrounds it
failureModes: aria-expanded on the panel instead of the trigger — it is the control's state
the panel hidden with height:0 or opacity, which hides it from nobody
a div as the trigger, so there is no role and no keyboard
aria-controls naming an id nobody built
api: AC.createDisclosure(root, options) -> { open, close, toggle, isOpen, destroy }
